label: Gross Revenue
description: Total sales value before returns and discounts are netted out. The top-line number for "how much did we sell," used as the denominator for most ratio metrics below.

label: Net Revenue
description: Gross revenue minus refunds and returns. What actually lands as sales after customers send things back — the number that should be used for any margin calculation, not gross_revenue.

label: Average Order Value (AOV)
description: Net revenue divided by number of distinct orders. Furniture/homeware AOV is typically much higher than fashion or grocery retail because purchases are infrequent but large (a sofa vs. a t-shirt) — a sudden drop often means a mix shift toward small accessory items, not fewer big-ticket sales.
benchmark: SGD 150–400 for furniture/homeware; well below this suggests accessory-only baskets

label: Units Sold
description: Total item quantity sold, independent of price — useful for spotting volume moves that revenue alone can mask (e.g. a markdown driving units up while revenue stays flat).

label: Channel Mix Share
description: Each channel's (store / online / click-and-collect) share of net revenue. IKEA-style retailers watch this closely because a large swing (e.g. store share collapsing) usually signals an operational problem at that channel specifically, not a change in overall demand.

label: Revenue by Category
description: Net revenue broken down by product category (e.g. living room, kitchen, storage, bedroom, outdoor). The primary lens for "which part of the catalog is driving or dragging performance."

label: Return Rate
description: Refunded units as a share of units sold. Furniture returns are costly (bulky reverse logistics), so this is watched more tightly than in categories where returns are cheap to process.
benchmark: 3–8% typical for furniture/homeware; spikes usually trace to a specific SKU quality issue

label: Delivery/Assembly Attach Rate
description: Share of orders that add paid delivery and/or assembly service. A meaningful secondary revenue line for bulky furniture, and a leading indicator of operational strain if it drops sharply (customers opting out because promised delivery windows are unreliable).

label: Stock on Hand
description: Current inventory quantity by SKU. The base number every other inventory metric derives from.

label: Stockout Rate
description: Share of SKUs (within a category, weighted by normal sales volume) at zero stock. The single most important inventory metric for this business model — a stockout on a popular flat-pack item can silently erase a category's revenue for days before anyone notices in a manual review.

label: Days of Supply
description: Current stock divided by average daily sales velocity — "how many days until this SKU runs out at the current rate." Low values combined with a long supplier lead time (see supplier_lead_time_days) are the setup for a stockout before a reorder can land.
benchmark: 10–30 days typical; below the supplier lead time is a reorder-urgency signal

label: Inventory Turnover
description: COGS over a period divided by average inventory value — how many times stock "cycles" per year. Furniture retail turns much slower than fashion or grocery because items are large, expensive, and purchased infrequently; a falling turnover usually means dead stock building up, not a sales problem.

label: Dead Stock Value
description: Inventory value of SKUs with no sales in the last 90 days. Ties up warehouse space and working capital — a slow-moving companion metric to stockout_rate, watching the opposite failure mode: too much stock of the wrong things instead of too little of the right things.

label: Supplier Lead Time
description: Days between placing a purchase order and stock arriving, by supplier. The upstream trigger for most stockout incidents — a supplier slipping their normal lead time is often detectable before the resulting stockout shows up in sales.

label: Purchase Order Delay
description: Actual delivery date minus promised delivery date for open/recent POs. A more direct early-warning signal than lead time alone — flags a specific PO that's running late right now, which is what the Correlator needs to trace forward to an eventual stockout.

label: Reorder Point Breaches
description: Count of SKUs that have fallen below their configured reorder point without an open purchase order to replenish them. A direct operational gap — this is a SKU someone should have already reordered and hasn't.

label: Damage/Shrinkage Rate
description: Units written off as damaged or missing, as a share of units received. Flat-pack furniture has real in-transit and in-warehouse damage rates worth tracking separately from returns, since it's a supply-side loss rather than a customer decision.

label: Cost of Goods Sold
description: The direct cost of the inventory that was sold in the period. The main input, alongside net_revenue, for every margin metric below.

label: Gross Margin %
description: (Net revenue − COGS) / net revenue. The headline profitability metric — the one number that turns "we sold more" into "we made more," since a revenue increase driven by discounting can still shrink this.

label: COGS as % of Revenue
description: The inverse view of gross margin — COGS divided by net revenue. Useful as its own metric because a creeping COGS ratio (rising unit costs from a supplier) can erode margin even while gross_margin_pct still looks acceptable at the aggregate level.

label: Discount Impact
description: Total revenue given up to discounts/markdowns in the period. Pairs with units_sold to catch the "discount that killed margin without lifting volume" pattern — revenue and units both need to move to justify a markdown; if only revenue drops and units don't rise, the discount didn't work.

label: Accounts Receivable Ageing
description: Value of customer invoices (B2B/trade accounts, if the business has them) overdue by bucket (30/60/90+ days). Mostly relevant if this retailer has trade/wholesale accounts alongside consumer sales; a blowout here is a cash-flow risk independent of sales performance.

label: Accounts Payable Ageing
description: Value of supplier bills by how overdue they are. Watched alongside ar_ageing for overall cash position, and as a signal of supplier relationship strain that could itself cause future lead-time slippage.

label: Net Cash Flow
description: Cash in from sales/collections minus cash out for purchases/bills paid, over the period. The bottom-line liquidity number the Correlator's dollar-impact chains ultimately need to reconcile against.

label: Operating Expense
description: Non-COGS operating costs (rent, staff, utilities, marketing) for the period. Context for margin analysis — a gross-margin dip caused by rising opex is a different story than one caused by COGS or discounting.
